data.final_week_advice: In the final week, focus on integrating concepts, practicing under timed conditions, and addressing any lingering misconceptions before the exam.
data.summary: This 3‑week plan tackles the student’s weak unit (Force and Translational Dynamics) first, then covers the remaining units in the middle week, and ends with a mixed review week. Each week uses the 7 available hours, includes concrete tasks, and incorporates the single live class available in week 1.

weeks.focus: Master force concepts and free‑body diagrams
tasks: Watch the live class on 2.2 and 2.5 and take detailed notes
Do 15 free‑body diagram practice problems, then self‑grade using the rubric
Solve 10 kinematics problems on displacement and velocity (1.2)
Create a 5‑minute video explaining how to set up a free‑body diagram for a sliding block

weeks.focus: Cover remaining units and apply concepts
tasks: Do 20 problems on kinetic energy and work (3.1,3.2) and check solutions
Solve 10 linear momentum problems (4.1) and record reasoning
Work through 5 rotational kinematics problems (5.1) and diagram each step
Complete 10 oscillation problems (7.1) focusing on energy conservation
Tackle 5 fluid density problems (8.1) and explain the concept in writing
Take a 60‑minute timed quiz covering all topics listed
Identify top 3 mistakes and write a brief reflection on each
Redo the most challenging problem from each topic
Create a summary sheet linking concepts across units
Schedule a 30‑minute mock exam session with a peer or tutor
